note: Bus grant (POL-BUS-01), wait states and the wait cap (POL-WAIT-01), the stop latch set by HLT and STPST (POL-HLT-01) and the HALTED state (POL-HLT-02). Unit conventions that no page prints (grant hold 1 cycle, release = config release_latency_cpu_cycles, HALTED 1 cycle, the STPST edge processed first at step start, then stop before BUSRQ before INTR before INTRM) rest on C40, C45, C52, C53 and C54, so these vectors are kind policy. Every vector that contains an interrupt entry answers IAB with $1004. Every expect value is read from the cited page image and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation.

vectors.cite: Bus request/acknowledge sequence figure, pdf 36; Fig 2-6, pdf 22; SC.6, pdf 25; interrupt sequence figure, pdf 35
vectors.derivation: Four units. The previous unit was interruptible (init prev_interruptible 1), no SDBD prefix is pending and BUSAK is clear. Step 1, BUSRQ and INTR both high: at an interruptible boundary Fig 2-6 (pdf 22) tests BUS REQUEST before INTERRUPT REQUEST, and pdf 25 says the CPU 'will honor Bus Requests before it will honor Interrupt Requests', so the step is a bus grant: no bus access (pdf 36, the bus floats, bus control NACT), BUSAK asserted, 1 cycle (POL-BUS-01 hold unit, C52). Step 2, BUSRQ still high: the CPU stays in the WAIT (NACT) loop of Fig 2-6, one more 1-cycle grant unit. Step 3, BUSRQ low: the release unit, which lasts the profile release latency of 2 cycles (config default release_latency_cpu_cycles 2, C52, inference from pdf 36), clears BUSAK and reports BUS_RELEASED. A grant does not change prev_interruptible (A-02): Fig 2-6 leaves the bus request loop into the interrupt request test, not into a fetch. Step 4, INTR high: the boundary is still the interruptible one, so INTR (always honoured, pdf 12) starts an interrupt entry at cycle 1 + 1 + 2 = 4. Entry (interrupt sequence figure, pdf 35; SC.6, pdf 24-25; POL-INT-04, C30): INTAK at cycle 0 of the unit puts out R6 (the flat test bus answers $0000, which the CPU ignores), NACT, DW at 2 and DWS at 3 write the current PC at R6, NACT, IAB at 5 inputs the service routine address into the PC, three NACT, so the unit is 9 cycles; R6 goes up by one after the store; IAB answers $1004 and loads all 16 bits of R7 (POL-IAB-01); flags are not pushed; prev_interruptible becomes 0 (Fig 2-6, pdf 22: the sequence returns to the fetch). INTAK at 4 with address $02F0; DW at 6 writes the PC $1000 at $02F0; R6 = $02F0 + 1 = $02F1; IAB at 9 answers $1004, so R7 = $1004. Cycles 1 + 1 + 2 + 9 = 13. Flags and INTFF stay 0; BUSAK ends 0. Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

vectors.cite: BDRDY, pdf 12; immediate table, MVII row, pdf 57; BDRDY timing figure, pdf 37; notes on BDRDY, pdf 40
vectors.asm: MVII #$1234, R1 (the instruction word at $1000 answers with 36 wait cycles)
vectors.derivation: One unit. The fetch at 0 from $1000 reads $02B9 (the record carries the word on the bus) and the device answers 36 wait cycles, one more than the profile cap bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles = 35 (pdf 12: the wait must stay under 40 microseconds; C53). The page defines no behaviour past the bound, so the policy is a sticky fault (POL-WAIT-01, D-12): the unit is abandoned with the architectural state as before it (R1 and R7 = $1000 unchanged, nothing decoded), run state FAULTED, fault reason BUS_WAIT_LIMIT, event FAULT, unit FAULT. The unit ends one cycle past the cap: the address cycle 1, the 35 accepted wait cycles and the cycle that exceeds the cap, 1 + 35 + 1 = 37 cycles (the core convention, inference). prev_interruptible stays 1; flags stay 0.
